The divergence distance primitive computes a scalar value representing how far ahead a branch is. This is used in conjunction with a license compliance check that filters out any content already present in the competitive-intel zip. The method/formula boundary primitive identifies unique intellectual constructs by comparing sets of methods across branches, main, and the zip. These primitives form a dual structure: one for tracking divergence and another for enforcing exclusivity. Failure modes include false positives from untracked commits or misclassified license tags. The system assumes repository consistency and complete metadata availability.
